title: Orchestrator drops non-bundle tool calls that lack request_id instead of returning the placeholder result
reasoning: The single-tool helper has explicit intended behavior for a missing request_id: it returns a successful placeholder ToolResult indicating local runtime execution is pending, and the included test verifies that contract. The orchestrator's non-bundle path bypasses that helper behavior by skipping such calls entirely, so callers through the normal orchestrator get fewer tool results than tool calls. In an LLM tool-call loop this can leave a requested tool without a corresponding result message, causing dropped work or protocol mismatch depending on the caller's expectations.
reproduction: Construct a ParsedResponse with one non-bundle ParsedToolCall whose metadata is None or lacks request_id, then call ToolResultOrchestrator.execute_tools_from_response with a session_ref. The returned ToolExecutionBatch will contain zero tool_results, whereas execute_single_tool on the same call would return the placeholder result tested in tests/backend/test_single_tool_execution.py.
recommendation: Remove the orchestrator-level skip and delegate all non-bundle calls to execute_single_tool, or make the orchestrator produce the same placeholder result for missing request_id calls. Keep one source of truth for this fallback behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test covers execute_single_tool directly, but there is no orchestrator-level test proving that missing-request_id fallback survives the normal execute_tools_from_response path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend test for ToolResultOrchestrator.execute_tools_from_response with a non-bundle tool call lacking request_id, asserting that one placeholder tool result is returned instead of dropping the call.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/tools/orchestrator.py plus an orchestrator regression test.
